1362	Something you don't cook in, like a refrigerator for example:

1363	a refrigerator is no problem, you wash it with water and that's it,

1364	clean it well, even with a toothbrush, there are those rubber seals,

1365	clean well the places that have holes

1366	and cracks you can't reach, and if you know chametz got in there,

1367	you can drip a few drops of bleach or

1368	Fantastik into it, which nullifies it, makes it unfit

1369	for a dog to eat, and then even if there is chametz there, it can

1370	stay, because this chametz is no longer fit for

1371	a dog to eat. Medications: a person who needs medication on Pesach,

1372	it depends which medications. First let's start with a sick person in

1373	danger: those medications he must take, because if

1374	he doesn't take them his life is in danger, there is no room for a question,

1375	even outright chametz he should eat, since saving a life overrides

1376	the whole Torah, unless he can obtain alternatives. You can

1377	ask the doctor whether there are medications kosher for Pesach

1378	as substitutes. Almost every medication has

1379	kosher-for-Pesach alternatives, but if there are none, or the other one

1380	is not as good in quality, then it is life-threatening, so

1381	that he not endanger his life, he may take any medication,

1382	even if it is chametz. But when it is a sick person who is not

1383	in danger, no, not a matter of danger to life, but he doesn't

1384	feel well, it depends whether this medication has no good

1385	taste, like pills that you swallow, which if someone tries to suck on them

1386	their taste is not tasty, it is permitted to take them on Pesach even

1387	if they are chametz. Why? Because he doesn't feel the taste

1388	in them; they have no taste, he swallows them. If there are

1389	substitute medications, then certainly he shouldn't take chametz, he should ask the doctor,

1390	but if this is what there is, it is permitted. If they have taste, like

1391	lozenges for sucking, in that case one must make sure they are kosher

1392	for Pesach, because a sick person who is not in danger is forbidden to take

1393	pills or syrup that have a good

1394	taste when they are chametz. And as we said, there is always the

1395	alternative. On the night of the 14th, that is, next Thursday,

1396	we search for the chametz by the light of

1397	a candle. You leave the lights on in the house, but

1398	after the day gets dark, you take a candle. In the siddur there is a
